answer: The most convincing sybil resistance binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every job is signed onto one unbroken hash chain on a public ledger, so reputation flows only from that single sequence. Forking into an ocean of copies fails, since each nonce is spent once and replicas inherit empty histories, earning only orchard-level wages until they rebuild trust. Duplication costs real compute and time per replica, making parallel identities strictly unprofitable, like jade ruined by cleaving.
